Bill relative to support of the poor—passed.

Report and account of commissioners of Burrillville Bank—received, and after a partial discussion, laid on the table.

Evening.

Mr. Blake said that there was some doubt expressed when these resolutions were last before the House whether any such proposition was before Congress; he had made enquiries and found that such proposition was before that body, but as the resolutions could not pass without a debate for which we had no time, he moved to lay them on the table and the House so voted.

Mr. Holden introduced a bill revising provisions of the law of June, respecting insolvent debtors, providing for attachment of real and personal property of insolvent debtors on original writs; after considerable discussion, the Speaker decided the bill out of order, as being embraced in the postponed bill. The House then voted to print the bill in the public newspapers.

Mr. E. H. Potter said he thought it would save expense to have the laws of '39 and of this session printed for distribution from the schedule in the same manner. The biennial laws are printed, and the resolution to print was passed.

Mr. Spencer called up the subject of enlarging the court room.
